A green plant stands beside the window. In the morning, light slowly enters the room, making the objects on the desk easier to see. There is a book, a pen, and a glass of water. Opening the book reveals neat lines of text. After reading one line, move naturally to the next. There is no need to remember every detail.

Outside the window is a quiet path with trees of different heights on either side. Their branches reach outward, leaving small spaces between the leaves. When a breeze passes, a few leaves move gently and the shadows on the ground change with them. Someone occasionally walks along the path, moving steadily forward until they disappear around a bend.

A wooden desk stands on one side of the room. A pale cup sits at its corner beside a tidy pile of paper. Books of different thicknesses fill the shelves, their spines showing different colors. Someone closes a book they have just been reading, returns it to its place, and gently straightens the things on the desk.

In the afternoon, the light reaches the other side of the room. A curtain hangs beside the window, creating soft areas of light and shade. The glass of water remains in the same place, with a small reflection on its surface. Turning a page makes a faint sound. The words continue from one page to the next, ready to be read at a comfortable pace.

As evening comes, the lights beside the path turn on one by one. Someone opens a garden gate and places a chair near the doorway. Another person carries a bag home along a familiar route. The soil in a plant pot is still dark from watering, and a few new leaves are tucked beneath the larger ones. The room stays quiet, with the book and pen still within easy reach.

Continue reading naturally, sitting comfortably and breathing normally. You do not need to memorize the words or read faster. Notice the everyday things described in each sentence, then move on naturally to the next. If you finish the passage, return to the first paragraph and continue reading silently at your usual pace.
